lines.en: label day237:
scene watabesan1
I sit at my desk and begin to sort through a large packet of paperwork that was left for me by one of the[school] administrators.
I’m not sure why they didn’t just send out an email with all of this information, but I’ve come to accept that nothing about this[school] is normal as-is, so why start changing that now?
Still, though, who would have thought simply transferring a bunch of students from one[school] to another would be such an issue?
Oh, did I forget to mention that?
Right.
Following the collapse of the[school] in the more urban section of town, students were given a number of options.
The first (And probably the best option) was to simply attend a virtual classroom sort of thing until a new[school] could be constructed.
The second option, which a bunch of fucking idiots must have chosen because who would pass up the chance to learn from their bedroom?-
Was the opportunity to transfer[school]s and carry out the rest of their education in none other than [kumon_mi_high].
Also, why is this[school] the one named [kumon_mi_high] when the other one is also in Kumon-mi as well?
This is stupid.
I close the packet and lean back in my chair, waiting for something interesting to happen as I always do.
Something interesting happens right away.
Sweet.
: Come in.
scene watabesan2
: I want to fucking die.
: That’s...cool?
: Do we know each other?
: Not really.
: Then why did you come to see me?
: All of the other teachers left for the day and I needed someone to complain to.
: Other teachers?
: So you’re a teacher as well?
: Wakana Watabe.
: You inherited two of the misfits from my class and I never had the chance to thank you.
: Oh, Molly and Tsuneyo’s old teacher. You’re welcome, I guess.
: I want to fucking die.
: Yeah, you mentioned that when you first walked in.
scene watabesan3
: Really, though...Why now?
: Things would have been so much easier if everyone just died when that stupid[school] sunk into the ground.
: We’re all going to die anyway, no point in sticking around and trying to avoid that.
: I want to say that isn’t a very teacher-like thing to say, but I’m in the same boat.
scene watabesan4
: So you also wake up every morning and struggle to get out of bed and resign yourself to yet another miserable day of misery and...misery?
: More or less, yeah.
: Then I shall confide in you from now on as no one else seems to understand me in this god-forsaken[school].
: That’s fine I guess. Count me in.
scene watabesan5
: I will begin to draft our double-suicide note right away.
: Okay, maybe don’t count me in. I didn’t realize that’s what I was signing up for.
: I want to fucking die.
It seems this transfer-process has really started weighing on Ms. Watabe.
Or she’s just like this all the time.
I really have no idea.
scene watabesan6
: Can I count on you to take all of the weird girls out of my class if we’re really going to be doing this transfer-thing?
: My room is already full of pathetic miscreants and I’ve heard that you handle that type of student well.
: What? Where did you hear that?
: Teenage girls talk too much. It’s annoying.
: I hear a bunch of things about the operation you’re running.
: It also sounds a lot like you could get fired if any part of it is true.
: You’re not going to rat me out if I don’t agree to taking on your “miscreants,” are you?
: Oh, not at all. Do you have any idea how long and arduous that process would be?
: Even showing up to[school] takes more energy than I’m willing to expend.
: So it’s fine if you continue being a horrible excuse for a teacher. I’m not going to do anything about it.
: Well...Thanks then, Ms. Watabe.
: Wakana, please.
: Then thanks, Wakana.
: And how should I refer to you? Arakawa?
: Just Sensei is fine.
: Oh, you're serious?
: I thought there was a joke coming.
: For a moment, I almost even looked forward to it.
: Do you...like jokes?
: I don’t like anything.
: I just want to sleep forever and never have to teach again.
: Why even become a teacher?
: Who knows?
: I’d ask you the same question but I’m pretty sure it’s the same reason all [young]men become teachers.
: I’m not that bad...
: You’re not?
: Sensei! Are you available right now? There’s something I need to talk to you about.
Ah, there we go. I’m sure Makoto will be willing to vouch for me and make me sound like less of the...person I actually am to this other educational-professional.
: Watch this. My class-rep will vouch for me.
: What? I can’t just leave?
: Didn’t you come in here to complain? Where’s the harm in killing a little more time?
: Umm...Are you going to answer me or should I just come back later?
: Sorry, Makoto. Come on in.
scene watabesan7
Makoto walks in and drops an even larger stack of papers on my desk.
My sanity begins to slip away and I contemplate taking up a suicide pact with Wakana after all.
: Oh. Ms. Watabe is here.
: Are any of us really here?
scene watabesan8
: Are the two of you friends? I can’t say I’ve ever seen you together before.
: This is our first time meeting but I’m pretty sure the two of us are going to die together.
: No. We’re all going to die alone.
: I’m a little shocked by the eerily good chemistry between you two, but I’m just going to chalk it up to end-of-day woes.
: Life itself is woe. Never-ending woe.
: The transfer thing is really getting to you two, huh?
: That’s actually why I’m here. I just wanted to make sure you-
: Wait, before that, I need you to confirm to Ms. Watabe that I am not a horrible teacher.
scene watabesan9
: Are you in danger, Miyamura?
: He hasn’t put a collar on you yet, has he?
One day...
: A...collar?
: May I inquire as to what this is all about?
: I’m just trying to protect the girls of this[school].
: You called your entire class miscreants like five minutes ago and openly hate your job.
scene watabesan10
: Uh...I’m not quite sure what’s going on here...but Sensei isn’t nearly as bad as the rumors suggest.
: He’s not?
: What rumors are even being circulated about me?
: I only converse with the girls in my class and not any of the teachers, so I don’t even-
: Oh, okay. I think I get it.
scene watabesan11
: It’s fine. If Miyamura says you’re a good teacher, I have no reason to disbelieve her.
: She’s one of the only good students I know.
: I even tried to poach her for my class but she vehemently refused, electing to keep fixing your mistakes instead.
: You tried to steal one of my students without even telling me?
: Just the one. To make up for it, you can have anyone from my class that you like.
: Twelve is already way too much for me.
: Pathetic. I have thirty and I’m about to get even more.
: Jesus. How big is your classroom?
: Too fucking big. Get me out of this hell, please.
scene watabesan12
: Oh, apologies for the language, Miyamura.
: I don’t often get to talk with people my own age, so I must have let my true self slip for a moment.
: Oh, I don’t mind. Sensei speaks like that all the time.
scene watabesan13
: He does, does he?
scene watabesan14
: Oh, n-not in[school], of course! I just mean when the two of us are together after[school]!
: You hang out and curse with your students after[school]?
: Thanks, Makoto. You really helped clear my name for me.
scene watabesan15
: Hah...
: Not like it really matters to me...
: No point in putting any effort into anything when we’re all just going to get sucked into the void when we least expect it.
: Does that mean you’ll be coming back to complain to me more often from now on?
scene watabesan16
: Agreeing would imply that I put actual thought into my actions.
: Is that...not a thing you normally do?
: It’s not.
: Why bother putting thought into anything when-
: We’re all just going to die anyway, right?
: Right.
: See? You’re starting to get it.
: As...much as I’d hate to interrupt...whatever is happening right now, I do need to start going over the transfer process with you, Sensei.
: It’s a little different this time given the amount of girls who will be moving into the[school].
: Maybe Ms. Watabe can stay around to hear your explanation as well? I know she’s struggling too.
: I’m not struggling with this, I just hate it.
: I finally had some time to breathe with Molly leaving and now I have to deal with even more transfer students. What if they’re worse?
: Just so you’re aware, the transfers are coming from Kumon-mi, not Dublin.
: I don't think Molly's country of origin has any bearing on her-
: I don’t care where they’re coming from. I just want them to shut up and do their fucking work.
scene watabesan17
: Oh. Sorry again, Miyamura.
: You shouldn’t have to hear that.
: It’s fine...I even feel like I learned a thing or two about you today, Ms. Watabe.
: Does this mean you’ll leave this man and come keep my class in-line instead of his?
: At least be considerate enough to not do this in front of me. Poach her behind my back.
scene watabesan18
: Didn’t you just complain about me doing that a minute or two ago? Give me a break.
: Again...I’d really like to go over this transfer thing sooner rather than later...
scene watabesan19
: Of course...I need to get going anyway...
: Big plans, Wakana?
: Yes. Sleeping for the next sixteen hours.
: Good day, Miyamura. Sensei...
scene watabesan20
Ms. Watabe leaves and things suddenly become normal again with one less dark cloud floating around in my office.
: Wakana?...
: You two are on a first-name basis now?
: It appears that way.
: Ahh...It feels like just the other day, a certain student-council president suffered a panic attack when I referred to her by her first name.
scene watabesan21
: O-Obviously! You just started doing it out of nowhere one day and I had to learn to adapt!
: I haven’t freaked out about that in a long time, Sensei!
: Yeah, because now we have sex.
scene watabesan22
: Ugh...Can we just go over this packet now? I’m not in the mood to discuss our weird relationship dynamic today.
: Can you give me the watered-down version and just omit the stuff you’re going to do yourself?
scene watabesan23
: That’s...pretty much everything, though.
: Cool. Well, thanks for stopping by then. See you later, Makoto.
scene watabesan24
: Can I at least warn you that we’re going to be getting our first new girl this week?
: That soon?
: Do you know who she is yet?
scene watabesan23
: A girl named Uta Ushibori. I looked into her file and she’s not...the brightest.
: She’s not quite as far behind as someone like Miku, but she’s definitely not up to par with the rest of us.
: How do you even gauge everyone’s level when I’ve stopped assigning work?
: Keeping track of everyone’s level is the mark of a good teacher. I need to pay attention to things like this or I’ll never make it anywhere in life.
: You’re still thinking of becoming a teacher?
: Of course. Have I ever expressed any doubt that would contradict that?
: I...guess not.
: Huh.
: Well anyway, Uta should be showing up sometime over the next few days along with the first “batch” of new girls.
: There are quite a few of them given that their former[school] was rather large, so most classes will see sizable increases in the near future.
: We’ll only be receiving Uta with the first wave, though.
: Really? The[school] is getting that many new girls and we’re only getting one?
: Is that actually disappointing to-
scene watabesan25
: Don’t tell me you’re thinking of expanding your harem during a time like this?...
: Do you have any idea how much was lost in the collapse? Millions of Yen and personal belongings, Sensei.
: Granted, one of the girls who went there comes from an extremely wealthy family, so it’s already being rebuilt...but still.
: Show some consideration for everyone, please.
: For all we know, this Uta girl might seriously be struggling with that.
: Then I’m sure she’ll be pleased to find out that her life is about to get a hell of a lot easier.
: Or exponentially more difficult if she’s anything like me.
: She’s probably not. You’re kind of one-in-a-million, Makoto.
scene watabesan26
: Heheh~ I’m going to go out on a limb and assume you mean that as a compliment so I don’t have to strangle you with your stupid, brightly-colored tie.
scene black
$ day237 = True
